newsitem.title: UK: Ecuador agrees contract for oil pipeline expansion.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador agrees contract for oil pipeline expansion.

text.p: Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador has reached an agreement with five foreign oil companies for a $120 million project to expand the capacity of the Trans-Ecuadorean oil pipeline, a Petroecuador official said on Tuesday.

"Last Friday it was possible to reach an agreement with five major oil companies for investment and construction over the next 12 months," Miguel Montalvol, general coordinator for the company's petroleum construction unit told an industry conference.
He did not reveal which companies were involved.

The project will increase pipeline capacity from 320,000 barrels a day (bpd) at present to 410,000 bpd in 12 months and 480,000 bpd by the end of 1998, Montalvol told the annual Centre for Global Energy Studies conference.
Ecuador, Latin America's third largest oil exporter, currently pumps some 390,000 bpd of crude with about 70,000 bpd transported in the Trans-Andes pipeline.
The larger pipeline would allow Petroecuador to develop new fields in the Amazon Basin.
The project includes plans for additional tank capacity and an offshore buoy to load tankers of up to 250,000 tonnes.
